title: Logo demo clicks dead in Chromium post-huu: live-view button at y≈594 vs replay y≈341 — Run/Clear/slider never route (root receives the event, headless routing works)

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text:
Evidence (2026-10-17, wt-b4 during tambor-ibh): after the gallery fixture de-defness fix (gallery.html pointer-events:none removed), keyed-table/todo/counter/dropdown/select clicks work in Chromium — but all three LOGO interaction tests fail (gallery.spec Run appends / Clear world / slider rewinds).
Facts pinned by a temporary Playwright diagnostic (since removed):
- The drawn root RECEIVES the pointerdown (capture listener fired; target BUTTON; clientX 28.86, clientY 639) — delivery is fine.
- Mapped view point = (20.9, 594) (root rect (8,45,300,800)); the Run button's DOM box = (8,625,41x28) -> view y 580-608, so the mapped point is inside the DOM button's box.
- Headless routing WORKS: tests/bench-logo-route.test.ts dispatches mouse-down at buttonPoint(demoView("logo"), "Run") and gets non-empty intents (commit on record).
- KEY DIVERGENCE: the replayed (unit-metric) view places Run at view point (7.5, 341.5) while the browser's live view emits the DOM button at view y≈580 — a ~250px replay-vs-live vertical divergence for the logo demo only (multiline program listing measured by domMeasure vs unit measure is the prime suspect: canvas.ts/inspector heights accumulate).
- No console output at all on click (no unknown-effect tap, no worker error); LOGOLOG empty; worker load errors are invisible to page.on(console) (worker console is not piped) — the worker-response path (run-applied) is not yet ruled out.
Suspects ranked: (1) live-view vs replay divergence means some ROUTE input uses the replay/initial layout rather than the live view for logo (makeOpsApp view caching? the wrapped layout derived once?); (2) wrapOn inner-layer routing with the logo's bounds-after-metrics; (3) worker response hang (in-thread fallback DID work in jsdom bundle smoke, so less likely).
Repro: npx playwright test -c tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --project desktop -g "Run appends" (annotated test.fail in gallery.spec until fixed).

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text:
Root cause corrected (live-evidence tapped, not the routing theory in the description): the Run click always routed (mouse-down at view (20.86,594) -> intents:1) and the worker loaded and replied ok within 300ms (launch [1,true] -> reply {id:1,ok:true}). The bug was downstream: the async reply applied through the demo's INTERNAL opsApp.dispatch, outside the mount wire — and only wireSurface's route ever called backend.draw. Applied state was never re-rendered; the screen stayed at 0/0 'running' forever. Headless tests assert state, not the draw, so routing tests passed.

Fix (61d-feel, committed on main): mount.ts wraps app.dispatch so every applied batch re-renders (event path stays single-draw via a routed flag); logo.ts routes the reply through the demo's own public dispatch incl. a typed failure reply on runner rejection. Verified: 3 gallery.spec logo tests un-annotated and green in Chromium (Run 1/1, Clear 0/0, slider 3->0->2), screenshots regenerated (spiral + 1/1 visible), vitest 456/456, tsc clean, playwright 49 passed + 3 skipped (6 annotated risks findings unchanged), ah check 0 findings.

title: render: real-DOM backend layout parity — root anchoring + bare-group superposition
description:
HITL finding from tambor-y9d.4 (34 screenshots, user-confirmed scrambled; REAL index.html affected, not just the e2e fixture — reproduced headless at /tmp/real-index-todo.png).

Two defects in the real-DOM emission path (src/render/dom.ts + mount seam):

1. DRAWN ROOT NOT ANCHORED: the container the DomBackend builds into has no position:relative, so corpus translate wrappers (position:absolute;left/top) anchor to the initial containing block — demo content escapes #app and overlays the page header. Every gallery demo is affected on the live page.

2. BARE-GROUP SEMANTICS DIVERGE FROM CANVAS: the group builder appends children in flow (for child of node.drawables -> ctx.build(child, el)), but the corpus draw model composes bare sequences SUPERIMPOSED at the same origin — canvas/text backends paint each child at the current origin. DOM output diverges visually: in-flow labels/buttons/rects stack as text lines while translated siblings overlap them ('addcomplete' overdraw, '-5' label over the minus button, logo demo column pile-up).

jsdom contract tests pass because they assert structure, never layout.

FIX: root anchoring (position:relative on the backend root / mount container) + group children positioned absolute at the parent's origin (or an equivalent semantics-preserving emission); visual parity asserted by a Playwright test: drawn root bounding box inside #app, and no bounding-box intersection between a button and a same-origin sibling label.

METER: playwright visual test green + full vitest suite + ah check 0 findings + HITL re-pass on a regenerated screenshot set.

ANTI-GOALS: no changes to canvas/text backend draw semantics; no corpus reinterpretation — the fix lives in the DOM backend's real-DOM emission. Root-cause evidence: draw-tree dump shows todo view = wrap > [button, translate(30,10) ...] — the button is at group origin, the checkbox at (30,10): same-origin composition.

title: Ephemeral state lane for 60 Hz interaction state (pan/drag/scroll)
description: I13 from the chat-repo cold read (BZ2/BZ3 failure hypotheses: re-deriving the whole view while panning; copying point data). Design + implement a lane where high-frequency interaction state (pan offsets, drag positions, scroll) lives OUTSIDE the persistent/history state so 60Hz pointer streams do not enter history or trigger full re-derivation. Design-first ticket: define the state shape and which APIs read it before touching dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: drag/pan interaction demonstrably does NOT enter the persistent history (replay test); 60Hz pointer-move benchmark shows no per-event full re-derivation; design note recorded in the corpus or docs
notes:
Meter note: the 60Hz pointer-stream benchmark needs a concrete home before implementation — either a standalone microbench (preferred; does not need 54j.4's full harness) or the harness. Design-first lane: this is a design/semantics ticket (state shape, which APIs read the lane) — do not schedule AFK until the design note is recorded and reviewed.
Design note recorded: docs/design/ephemeral-interaction-lane.md (2026-10-20, revised after Rule-of-5 review with 3 TypeSafe-verified findings @0.97/0.92/0.93). Corrected premises: (a) 8xm no-op skip does NOT apply to lane effects (they are intents -> full draw per event) - lane needs its own draw boundary; (b) event model ALREADY delivers mouse-move (first-match) - no event-model spec change needed, the mount surface just never delivers pointermove (surface-input.ts tracks lastPos only); (c) per-app lane reaches effects via the EffectContext extra-keys seam, not the global registry. Phased plan: P0 mount pointer-move delivery -> P1 lane store + [lane,key,fn] effect (corpus spec interaction-lane) -> P2 lane-aware transform draw boundary -> P3 replay test + 60Hz microbench (derive-span count primary, paired measurement) -> P4 child: drag overlay + 54j.10 spatial index. Edge rulings: mid-drag state change forces full derive+draw (state wins structure, lane wins position); single-drag scope v1; hover stays separate; replay recorder excludes lane-typed effects.
Correction to the design note (self-caught before implementation): Phase 0 was ALREADY DONE by prior art — backend.attach (src/render/dom.ts:141, canvas.ts:222, mount.ts:177) forwards pointermove as mouse-move through normalizeDOMEvent -> deliver -> router, proven live by the existing 'pointermove carries the button-down state (drag vs hover)' test. surface-input.ts's own pointermove listener is only lastPos tracking for the synthetic cancel mouse-up; the two coexist. My CORR-002 generalization ('surface swallows moves') was wrong for the integration layer — it holds only for the headless synthetic tap path (tapEvents returns [] for drags, which is about synthetic down/up pairs, not moves). Work starts at Phase 1: lane store + [lane,key,fn] effect via EffectContext extra-keys seam. Design note updated in docs/design/ephemeral-interaction-lane.md.
PHASE 1 LANDED, pushed cb6e1fd through all gates (espectacular-contracts 70s, testaruda-exec green, pretender full, docs stamp). Phase 0 confirmed done by prior art (backend.attach pointermove forwarding). Phase 1 (this push): new spec openspec/specs/interaction-lane/spec.md (4 invariants: lane_outside_state, lane_update_semantics, lane_ctx_reachable, lane_batch_no_repaint; 5 contracts p-ctx-lane/p-lane-update/p-mixed-batch/p-no-repaint/p-state-identity, ah check 744/0); makeApp owns a per-app lane store threaded via the EffectContext extra-keys seam; ['lane',key,updateFn] applies registry-style BEFORE any state handler so custom handlers (undo history, external stores) cannot drop lane writes; lane-only batches schedule NO repaint (single_repaint untouched for state batches) so a 60Hz lane stream costs zero per-event re-derivation; App gains getLane(). Tests/effects-lane.test.ts red->green 5/5; vitest 702/702; tsc 0. Sideband: makeAppDispatch extracted (pretender 40-line floor) and the canvas-layer paired meter got a 30s budget (the >4s-under-load flake blocked pre-push, wave-3 pattern). REMAINING: Phase 2 lane-aware draw boundary (lane-only batch must not fall through to backend.draw(full tree) in wireSurface — transform draw over the cached tree, BZ2 pan-as-transform precedent; spec delta backend-render or interaction-lane); Phase 3 replay test (recorder excludes lane-typed effects; drag commits via pointer-up intent) + standalone 60Hz microbench (derive-span count primary, paired measurement per findings-8xm); Phase 4 child ticket: drag overlay + 54j.10 spatial index wiring.

title: Investigate full-suite load-flake family (parallel-worker jitter reds unrelated tests; p_keyboard_bridge recorded)
description:
Recurring pattern, recorded 4+ times in session notes (2026-10-18 54j.10/.11 wave, 2026-10-20 add-worker-reply-validation apply): tests that are green solo fail under the full vitest suite's parallel-worker load — different victims each run (p_swappable, p_touch_hover, phase-timers, spa-mount-input, view-bounds-memo, ui-mobile p_keyboard_bridge; playwright mobile-380 flakes are the same family). Standing ruling so far has been 'don't chase individually' — this ticket is the systematic investigation instead.

Hypotheses to test: (a) CPU/memory contention — full suite spawns max workers + fast-check properties + perf meters; a >4s test under load flakes (wave-3 gotcha: machine load ~5.7 makes all >4s vitest tests flaky); (b) shared module-level state across workers (never-reseeded tables, global id counters like worker_effect nextId); (c) timer/rAF fake-vs-real leakage between files in the same worker; (d) testaruda selection running a different subset shape than plain vitest (subset boundary changes worker packing).

Investigation shape: instrument one flake-prone run (vitest --reporter=verbose + --no-file-parallelism A/B), pair failing runs with machine-load samples, classify victims by root cause, and decide levers: worker-count cap, --pool=forks vs threads, test isolation (reseed on init), or per-test timeout budgets (the wave-3 precedent). Deliverable: a written ruling in benchmarks/ or docs/ + either a fix or an accepted-and-documented flake class with a gate policy.

## Context
Recorded instances: 2026-10-18 54j.11 wave (5 unrelated failures on first just test, green on rerun), 2026-10-18 8xm snap (playwright mobile-380 different flake each run), 2026-10-20 apply session (p_keyboard_bridge 1/2 runs under ah check --run-tests, green solo). comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text:
RESOLUTION (2026-10-14) — all three decisions made and implemented:

(1) Degenerate recall, 0 actual failures: VACUOUS PASS. Recall over an empty positives set is 1.0 by convention — a clean run gives no ranking evidence either way. Implemented upstream in testaruda PR #85 (merged ef325f6): CalibrationMetrics.vacuous flag + calibrate() prints "✓ CALIBRATED (vacuous — 0 actual failures; recall@k degenerate 0/0, nothing to rank)". Live-verified on tambor's store (329 hold-out, 0 failures, recall 1.000). Insufficient history (<2 runs) stays measured 0.0 + warning. Genuine miscalibration (failures > 0, recall < threshold) keeps NOT CALIBRATED.

(2) Silent NOT CALIBRATED: never. tools/gates/testaruda-exec.sh now captures exec output and enforces: NOT CALIBRATED + "Actual failures: 0" → explicit vacuous-pass note printed, tolerated (covers the pre-#85 engine too); NOT CALIBRATED with failures > 0 or unparseable output → exit 1 (blocks). All four paths shim-verified (vacuous→0, failures→1, unparseable→1, runfail→1). In practice failures > 0 never reaches a tolerated exit — exec propagates the runner's failure exit first — so the gate is advisory for selection quality but correctness paths already block.

(3) Id entity-escaping: fixed upstream via testaruda-uwup (PR #84, junit attr XML-unescape). Local exec: 0 unmatched (was 12; the 4-item residual was store staleness — discover+exec cycles to 0; exec re-discovers internally at push time).

Anti-goals respected: gate not weakened (vacuous case reasoned + explicit; genuine miscalibration now BLOCKS where it previously silently passed), store not gamed. CI half (60/333) remains testaruda-7r9l.
